primitives.name: Retinal Projection Duality
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our retina now holds the image which a cross of square shape throws when in front, but which a cross of the slant-legged pattern would throw, provided it were actually on the wall in the distant place at which we look.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I_{\\text{present}}': 'retinal image intensity (dimensionless)', 'I_{\\text{absent}}': 'imagined retinal image intensity (dimensionless)', 'S': 'object shape (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Perception arises from a superposition of present and absent retinal projections; shape constancy emerges from selective attention to one image class.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When retinal image ambiguity exceeds cognitive resolution threshold.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian inference maps present retinal image to posterior over object shapes; GSE state transition models belief update from I_present to I_absent.
layer2.telemetry: Perceptual constancy error rate vs. projected image angle.

primitives.name: Shape Constancy Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Why, when the objective cross gives us so many shapes, as it varies its position, should we think we feel the true shape only when the cross is directly in front?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'K_{\\text{shape}}': 'perceptual kernel for shape constancy (dimensionless)', '\\theta': 'angular deviation from frontal view (radians)', 'S_{\\text{true}}': 'true object shape (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Shape constancy is a derived kernel that selects dominant retinal image based on spatial alignment with prior expectations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At extreme angular deviations where projected image distortion exceeds perceptual tolerance.

layer2.mapping: GSE derives shape constancy from GSI's probabilistic shape posterior; GSI computes kernel weights from retinal image likelihoods.
layer2.telemetry: Angular deviation vs. reported shape accuracy.

primitives.name: Imagined Sensation Isomorphism
primitives.verbatim_quote: An imagined sensation, not a felt one, it is true, but none the less essentially and originally sensational or retinal for that, —the sensation, namely, which we should receive if a'real' slant-legged cross stood on the wall in front of us and threw its image on our eye.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I_{\\text{real}}': 'retinal image from real object (dimensionless)', 'I_{\\text{imagined}}': 'retinal image from imagined object (dimensionless)', 'F': 'perceptual fidelity (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Imagined sensations are isomorphic to real retinal inputs under identical geometric conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When imagined and real retinal images diverge beyond perceptual congruence limits.

layer2.mapping: GSI equates imagined and real retinal inputs via isomorphism; GSE models imagined sensation as a state transition from real to virtual.
layer2.telemetry: Fidelity of imagined vs. real retinal image match.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that visual perception involves a duality between present retinal input and imagined retinal projections. The 'slant-legged cross' example illustrates that the brain does not merely process what is seen, but also constructs hypothetical retinal images to infer object properties. This leads to a dual manifold: one of actual retinal projections and another of imagined ones. Shape constancy emerges as a kernel that selects the most probable shape from a set of possible retinal images, favoring those aligned with frontal viewing. The failure mode occurs when the discrepancy between real and imagined projections exceeds perceptual thresholds, causing misperception. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian inference over retinal image likelihoods; in GSE, it becomes a state transition driven by belief updates. The isomorphism between real and imagined sensations allows for consistent interpretation despite variable input.
